definitions.explanation: A point in time after the present or after a reference point.
The time to come; future circumstances.

examples.japanese: {後|のち}ほど{連絡|れんらく}します。
{雨|あめ}の{後|のち}{晴|は}れるでしょう。
examples.english: It will probably clear up after the rain.

examples.japanese: {卒業|そつぎょう}{後|のち}、{海外|かいがい}に{行|い}った。
{事故|じこ}の{後|のち}、{安全|あんぜん}{対策|たいさく}が{見直|みなお}された。
examples.english: After the accident, safety measures were reviewed.

examples.japanese: {会議|かいぎ}の{後|のち}に、{詳|くわ}しい{報告|ほうこく}をいたします。
examples.english: I will give a detailed report after the meeting.

examples.japanese: {後|のち}のことは{考|かんが}えていない。
examples.english: I haven't thought about what comes later.

examples.japanese: {後|のち}の{世|よ}に{名|な}を{残|のこ}す。
examples.english: To leave one's name for future generations.
examples.notes: {後|のち}の{世|よ} = future generations, posterity

examples.japanese: {後|のち}に{大|おお}きな{問題|もんだい}になった。
examples.english: It became a big problem later on.

examples.japanese: この{決定|けってい}が{後|のち}にどんな{影響|えいきょう}を{与|あた}えるか、{今|いま}はまだ{分|わ}からない。
examples.english: We don't yet know what effect this decision will have in the future.

examples.japanese: あの{出来事|できごと}は、{後|のち}になって{振|ふ}り{返|かえ}ると、{大切|たいせつ}な{経験|けいけん}だったと{思|おも}う。
examples.english: Looking back on it later, I think that event was an important experience.

notes:
USAGE: {後|のち} is a more formal/literary way to say 'after' or 'later' compared to {後|あと}. It's commonly used in weather forecasts and formal writing.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・〜の{後|のち} (after ~)
・{後|のち}に (later, subsequently)
・{後|のち}ほど (later - polite)
・{後|のち}の{世|よ} (future generations, posterity)

WEATHER EXPRESSIONS:
・{雨|あめ}{後|のち}{曇|くも}り (rain, then cloudy)
・{晴|は}れ{後|のち}{雨|あめ} (clear, then rain)

CONTRAST:
・{後|のち} - afterwards (formal/literary)
・{後|あと} - after, later (everyday)
・{以後|いご} - after, since (formal)
・その{後|ご} - after that
